10. During the winter animals sit into curt, why?
Ans:- During winter, animals sit in a curled position to reduce the surface area exposed to cold air, helping them conserve
body heat and stay warm.
11. Two objects 'A' and 'B' have equal masses but the specific heat capacity of 'A' is greater than that of 'B'. Whose
temperature will increase more if 400 J of heat is supplied to each? Why?
Ans:- Object B will have a greater increase in temperature because it has a lower specific heat capacity, so the same amount
of heat raises its temperature more than that of object A.

13. In winter morning as soon as we wake up the air inside the room is cold but if we go out and return to the same room, we
feel warm, why?
Ans:- In the morning, the room air is cold because it has lost heat overnight. When we go out and return, our body is warmer
than the room, so the room feels warm in comparison.

16. An iron bar heats up when it is hammered continuously for some time. Why?
Ans:- An iron bar heats up when hammered continuously because the mechanical work done by hammering is converted into
heat energy, which raises the temperature of the bar.
17. The tea in an open tea cup becomes cold after sometime. The process of cooling the tea in the teacup stops after certain
time. Why?
Ans:- The tea in an open cup becomes cold due to loss of heat to the surrounding air. The cooling stops after some time
because the tea and the surrounding air reach thermal equilibrium, meaning their temperatures become equal.
18. Water pipe crack in cold places in the winter. Why?
Ans:- Water pipes crack in cold places during winter because water freezes and expands as its temperature drops below 0°C,
exerting pressure on the pipe and causing it to burst.
